title: RNA roles in gene expression
caption: One transcription system supplies distinct RNA products. mRNA specifies the protein; tRNA links codons with amino acids; rRNA organizes the ribosome; snRNA and snoRNA assist RNA maturation.

title: Antiparallel RNA hairpin
caption: The sequence 5′-GCGAAACGC-3′ forms three possible antiparallel Watson–Crick pairs and a three-residue loop. Dashed lines denote pairing, not backbone bonds.

title: Assembly versus RNA abundance
caption: A transcribed RNA can bind proteins and form an active RNP; a defective binding interface may yield detectable RNA but no functional particle.

title: Old ribosomes and new RNA
caption: Conceptual isotope-label logic: newly synthesized labelled RNA associates with older distinguishable ribosomes. Labels indicate age, not RNA sequence or covalent attachment.

title: Typical mature nuclear mRNA
caption: Schematic mature eukaryotic message: the 5′ cap and poly(A) tail are not translated as part of the main coding region. The stop codon ends the coding frame; sizes are not to scale.

title: Monocistronic and polycistronic messages
caption: The upper model contains separate coding regions A, B and C on one RNA, each able to support a separate product. The lower model represents one major coding region.

title: RNA remaining after synthesis stops
caption: Illustrative first-order decay for 10- and 20-minute half-lives. Curves begin at equal abundance and diverge because removal rates differ; axes show fraction of initial RNA and elapsed minutes.

title: Bacterial and eukaryotic cytoplasmic rRNAs
caption: Conventional bacterial 70S has 30S (16S) and 50S (23S, 5S) particles; mammalian cytoplasmic 80S has 40S (18S) and 60S (28S, 5.8S, 5S). Svedberg coefficients are nonadditive.

title: Mammalian pre-rRNA and independent 5S synthesis
caption: Pol I makes a precursor containing 18S, 5.8S and 28S regions. Spacers are removed during maturation. Pol III supplies 5S separately; one of each is used in an assembled ribosome.

title: Canonical tRNA secondary structure
caption: A schematic cloverleaf: the 5′ and 3′ ends pair in the acceptor stem; CCA is at the 3′ end; the D, anticodon and T arms branch from the core. The variable region is between anticodon and T arms.

title: tRNA tertiary geometry and anticodon orientation
caption: The two ends of the L-shaped adaptor serve distinct tasks. The 3′ amino acid attachment site and anticodon are separated in space. The codon and anticodon pair antiparallel.

title: Changing snRNA interactions in the major spliceosome
caption: Early U1 and U2 interactions recognize the 5′ splice site and branch region. U4 initially pairs with U6; release of U4 enables active U2/U6 contacts and U5 helps position exons.

title: C/D box guide positioning
caption: In the canonical C/D model, the target nucleotide pairs with the fifth guide residue upstream of the D box. Fibrillarin supplies methyltransferase activity.

title: H/ACA pseudouridylation pocket
caption: The guide hairpin interacts with sequences on either side of a target uridine. The selected U is exposed in the pocket and can be isomerized by the associated pseudouridine synthase.

title: Nuclear production and cytoplasmic use
caption: Typical eukaryotic cellular map: snRNA supports pre-mRNA splicing; snoRNA guides pre-rRNA maturation; tRNA matures and is exported. The mature RNA classes converge on cytoplasmic translation.
